findings.title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` causes template rendering to fail
findings.body: Line 6 closes the `if` block with `<%- end if %>`, which is invalid Ruby syntax (`end` followed by an incomplete `if` modifier with no expression). In Ruby/ERB, conditional blocks are closed with `end`, not `end if`. Rendering `embed/best.html.erb` will raise a `SyntaxError` whenever a topic embed is found and displayed.

findings.title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses all HTML sanitization, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without passing through `PrettyText.cook` or any HTML sanitizer. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using raw HTML from RSS/Atom feeds (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` unescapes feed item content directly via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without sanitization), and any user who can later edit that post (or any post with `cook_method == raw_html`) can also inject arbitrary `<script>` tags or event handlers that will be stored in `cooked` and rendered unescaped to all viewers.

findings.title: Unvalidated `embed_url` passed to `Kernel#open` allows SSRF and arbitrary command/file read
findings.body: In `EmbedController#best`, the user-supplied `params[:embed_url]` is enqueued to `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which does not restrict the URI scheme or port (for example, `ftp://`, `gopher://`, or arbitrary internal ports if the host resolves Internally or via DNS rebinding), and in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (which is also callable directly) `open(url).read` uses `Kernel#open` (`open-uri`). If `import_remote` is ever called with a string starting with `|` or a `file://` URL, `Kernel#open` will execute a shell command or read local files. Even through `TopicRetriever`, `URI.parse` allows any scheme with a matching host. `embed_url` should be restricted to `http`/`https` schemes and fetched with an HTTP client rather than `Kernel#open`.

findings.title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript string literal allows XSS
findings.body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `request.referer` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted JavaScript string: `'<%= request.referer %>'`. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Because `URI.parse` allows single quotes in the path or query string (or in browsers that do not percent-encode them in the `Referer` header), a referer such as `http://<embeddable_host>/?a='+alert(1)+'` will break out of the JS string literal and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Discourse origin. Use `.to_json` (or pass the origin constructed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) instead of raw ERB interpolation.

findings.title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that use `<description>`, causing `NoMethodError`
findings.body: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, line 35 calls `i.content.scrub`. In `SimpleRSS`, `item.content` only maps to Atom `<content>` or `<content:encoded>`; standard RSS 2.0 items that only provide `<description>` have `i.content == nil` (with the body in `i.description`). Calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the entire feed poll.

findings.title: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place
findings.body: Line 13 uses `contents << ...` to append the 'Imported from' footer, mutating the string argument in place. If the caller passes a frozen string, this raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`; if the caller reuses the string (as in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`), the footer is appended multiple times. Use `contents = "#{contents}..."` or `contents + ...` instead.
